title: Control moves closer to execution
dek: Five developments across organization-managed coding agents, supplier concentration, governed web retrieval, stateful streaming, and production-agent measurement—each tested for novelty and practical consequence.
cover_alt: Salesforce Agentic Enterprise Index editorial illustration
cover_caption: Production-agent telemetry is beginning to reveal distinct deployment shapes rather than one universal maturity path. Image: Salesforce.
editor_note: Novelty gate: this edition excludes category-level launch claims. Bedrock Web Search is labeled a material GA distribution update; organization-managed Copilot agents, stateful BigQuery continuous queries, and longitudinal agent telemetry are meaningful extensions; Cursor’s cutoff is treated as a supplier-risk event, not a new technical category.

developments.label: Organization control
developments.title: Shared coding agents become an organization-managed product surface
developments.what: GitHub’s August 28 Visual Studio update lets organization and enterprise owners publish custom agents across repositories. Developers can see each agent’s description and organizational source in the picker; the release also adds low, medium, and high reasoning effort, clearer model capability and cost information, and review of commits or uncommitted changes through the Git agent before a pull request.
developments.new: The meaningful extension is centralized distribution of specialized agents plus explicit reasoning-cost controls inside the IDE. The capabilities reach every Copilot plan, although sharing requires a GitHub organization.
developments.not_new: Repository instructions, assistants, model selectors, and automated review already exist in Copilot and Cursor. This packages familiar capabilities into a governable Visual Studio workflow; it does not invent coding agents.
developments.why: An agent can embody team policy but can also spread stale or unsafe instructions at organization scale. Reasoning effort turns quality, latency, and token consumption into explicit product and economic controls rather than hidden implementation details.
apply: Pilot one agent on a bounded job such as migration checks before organization-wide publication.
Assign an owner, version its instructions, and log acceptance, edit, and reversal rates.
Compare low and high effort on defect escape, latency, and cost per accepted change.
developments.caveat: Medium confidence; meaningful extension. GitHub provides no comparative quality, productivity, or cost results, so broader deployment should follow a measured pilot.

developments.label: Supplier risk
developments.title: Cursor’s model cutoff makes supplier concentration visible
developments.what: Cursor announced on August 14 that SpaceX had completed its acquisition, promising access to more compute and lower-cost in-house models. On August 28, OpenAI said it intended to wind down model supply to Cursor with a proposed November 12 cutoff; CNBC independently reported the planned termination.
developments.new: The new event is a concrete withdrawal date for a major upstream capability after a change of control. It converts a theoretical dependency into a timed migration, customer-communication, and continuity problem.
developments.not_new: Deplatforming, supplier concentration, and multi-model routing are established concerns. The novelty is the commercial trigger and compressed transition window—not model portability as a concept.
developments.why: Supplier incentives can change after acquisitions or competitive moves. A model-neutral interface is not genuine portability when prompts, evaluations, latency targets, economics, and customer expectations are tuned to one provider.
apply: Route representative common, high-value, and worst-case tasks to the replacement stack; compare success, latency, refusals, and margin.
Inventory customer promises and contract terms that change with the provider.
Add change-of-control rights and transition assistance to critical-supplier reviews.
developments.caveat: High confidence for the announced cutoff; customer impact remains uncertain. Cursor can substitute models, change its product mix, or negotiate supply, so the event proves exposure rather than a predetermined outcome.

developments.label: GA distribution update
developments.title: Managed web grounding creates a separately governable retrieval boundary
developments.what: Amazon Bedrock Web Search is a built-in tool through which supported models can search an AWS-maintained index, optionally fetch pages, and return citations. IAM permissions can separately govern search, fetch, and external-web access; AWS also documents regional processing and CloudTrail monitoring.
developments.new: Bedrock now makes search grounding a managed primitive rather than a bespoke tool loop, with distinct controls for index search, cached fetch, and live external access. The important delta is operational packaging and governance within Bedrock.
developments.not_new: OpenAI web search, Gemini grounding, and third-party search APIs already provide current retrieval. This is a material GA and distribution update, not a new category.
developments.why: Teams can expose current information without allowing unconstrained browsing, but a displayed citation does not necessarily mean the full page was fetched: AWS says annotations may remain when fetch authorization fails. Retrieval state therefore belongs in telemetry and user-facing evidence design.
apply: Test index-only, cached-page, and live-web policies against the same evaluation set.
Distinguish snippet-level from page-level evidence in the interface and logs.
Measure unsupported claims, source quality, latency, and cost—not citation count alone.
developments.caveat: High confidence for documented operation; material GA rollout. Model and region support are constrained, and independent retrieval-quality comparisons are not available.

developments.label: Data infrastructure
developments.title: BigQuery adds state to continuous queries
developments.what: Google’s August 24–28 release roundup places stateful processing for BigQuery continuous queries in preview. Joins, aggregations, and window functions can now operate directly on streaming queries—for example, computing a rolling 30-minute metric for a downstream application or agent.
developments.new: BigQuery continuous queries move from simpler event-by-event processing toward maintaining context across time and streams. For existing BigQuery teams, that can reduce the number of separate systems required for some near-real-time features.
developments.not_new: Flink, Kafka Streams, Materialize, and other cloud services already process stateful streams. This is a BigQuery extension, not a new data architecture.
developments.why: Fraud detection, onboarding, usage limits, and retention outreach can react to sequences rather than isolated events. Faster execution also makes product decisions about lateness, window definitions, correction logic, and acceptable automated action more consequential.
apply: Prototype one reversible intervention rather than migrating a full pipeline.
Measure freshness and false-positive cost alongside infrastructure performance.
Retain a holdout so faster intervention is tested against customer outcomes.
developments.caveat: Medium confidence; meaningful extension. Preview reliability, sustained-load cost, and migration economics versus established stream processors remain unproven.

developments.label: Production telemetry
developments.title: Agent telemetry points to two deployment shapes—not one maturity ladder
developments.what: Salesforce’s August 7 Agentic Enterprise Index studies an aggregated cohort with agents active in production every month from February 2025 through April 2026. It distinguishes high-volume, narrow consumer workflows from lower-volume, multi-step deployments in operationally complex sectors, while reporting growth in agents per organization and completed ‘Agentic Work Units.’
developments.new: The useful empirical extension is longitudinal production telemetry suggesting that skill breadth and work volume may represent different deployment strategies rather than sequential rungs on one maturity model.
developments.not_new: Vendor usage indexes and ‘work completed’ metrics are established. Salesforce defines the unit on its own platform, and the study does not show that agents caused the commercial outcomes discussed around the data.
developments.why: A narrow, high-volume agent needs strong unit economics and exception handling; a multi-step regulated agent needs permissions, auditability, and recovery before scale. Comparing both on one adoption score hides the product decision.
apply: Segment the portfolio by task diversity, volume, reversibility, and exception cost.
Use cost per successful work unit for narrow flows and human-reviewed completion plus incident severity for complex ones.
Treat vendor-defined work units as hypotheses until they correlate with retained customer value and margin.
developments.caveat: Medium confidence; meaningful empirical extension. The cohort includes persistent Agentforce users, Salesforce controls the definitions, and survivorship and selection limit causal interpretation.
developments.image_alt: Salesforce chart showing agent conversation volume and escalation rate over time
developments.image_caption: Salesforce reports steady escalation rates as conversation volume rises. This is vendor telemetry from a selected platform cohort, not independent causal evidence. Source: Salesforce Agentic Enterprise Index.

technique.title: The supplier-exit drill
technique.problem: An abstraction layer may technically support several vendors while prompts, evaluations, contracts, operational procedures, and customer promises remain provider-specific. The drill turns claimed optionality into observed switching time and customer impact.

steps.title: Choose the exit event
steps.body: Test an immediate outage, a 30-day termination, or a 50% price increase. The scenario determines what continuity actually requires.

steps.title: Map dependencies
steps.body: Inventory models, APIs, embeddings, fine-tunes, safety filters, data residency, rate limits, contractual rights, and customer-facing claims.

steps.title: Select representative jobs
steps.body: Include the most common task, the highest-value task, and the worst credible failure. Average traffic alone will conceal the hard parts.

steps.title: Run the substitute
steps.body: Freeze the product version and measure task success, latency, cost, refusals, rework, and segment-specific regressions.

steps.title: Rehearse operations
steps.body: Revoke credentials, switch routing, validate logs, notify support and customers, and confirm rollback rather than stopping at an offline comparison.

steps.title: Make the concentration decision
steps.body: Fund portability gaps, accept concentration explicitly because the advantage exceeds exit cost, or renegotiate transition terms.

technique.example: A research product’s backup model matches aggregate answer scores but changes URL formatting, doubles p95 latency, and cannot meet the same regional-processing promise. The team must normalize citation objects, set provider-specific latency budgets, and revise contracts before it can honestly claim failover.
technique.use_when: Use when supplier loss would breach a customer promise, erase margin, or stop critical work; repeat after acquisitions, architectural changes, or contract renewals.
technique.avoid_when: Do not fund expensive portability for low-impact components with easy manual replacement. Concentration can be rational when its measured advantage exceeds the exit cost.
technique.failure_modes: Testing only output quality; ignoring legal and data terms; using nonrepresentative traffic; never exercising credential revocation; and describing materially degraded service as equivalent.

book.title: The Probabilistic Product
book.author: Christie Mealo
book.thesis: AI-native products require strategy designed for variable outputs, natural-language intent, and changing model supply; adding an AI feature to a deterministic product is not enough. Available chapters cover AI-native products, how AI works, and an ‘intent interface,’ while later strategy and data-moat chapters remain unavailable.
ideas: Probabilistic quality is a product property: teams need distributions, failure classes, and recovery paths rather than a binary acceptance test.
Intent changes the interface: users specify outcomes while the system chooses steps, making permissions and visible plans part of interaction design.

AI-native is architectural, not cosmetic: if removing the model leaves the value proposition intact, the product may be AI-assisted rather than AI-native—a useful distinction for cost and defensibility.
A data moat matters only when rights and feedback convert data into better outcomes. This is a hypothesis inferred from the planned chapter, not a summary of unavailable text.
book.audience: Product leaders separating an AI-native strategy from feature opportunism and designing around variable output quality.
book.limitation: This is based on publisher material and available early-release contents, not a full-book read. Unavailable strategy, economics, and moat sections make any verdict provisional.
book.verdict_reason: Read the available chapters if defining an AI-native thesis now; defer a definitive judgment until the later strategic and economic sections are complete.

foundation.title: One-way and two-way doors
foundation.original: Amazon’s 2015 shareholder letter distinguishes hard-to-reverse Type 1 decisions from reversible Type 2 decisions and warns against applying slow Type 1 processes to both.
foundation.holds: Bounded experiments can move quickly. Irreversible data use, contracts, or autonomous financial actions require stronger evidence, authority, and recovery planning.
foundation.misapplied: Teams often call code ‘reversible’ while ignoring migration cost, customer trust, data persistence, contractual lock-in, or regulatory exposure. Technical rollback is only one dimension of reversibility.
foundation.update: Score reversibility across technical rollback, data deletion, economic loss, customer remedy, and reputational recovery. Pair door type with observability: an action that is theoretically reversible but cannot be detected promptly still deserves caution.
foundation.question: Which part of this decision is genuinely reversible, within what time, and for whom?

patterns.title: Control is moving closer to execution
patterns.body: Organization-distributed agents, reasoning-effort settings, retrieval permissions, and stateful signals make governance part of the operating product rather than a policy applied afterward.

patterns.title: Portability must be demonstrated
patterns.body: A multi-model menu means little without measured substitution quality, economics, contractual continuity, and a customer-safe migration procedure.

patterns.title: Real-time capability requires decision design
patterns.body: Faster signals improve adaptation only when false-positive costs, holdouts, correction rules, and reversibility are explicit.

patterns.title: Agent measurement is specializing
patterns.body: Narrow high-volume work and complex multi-step work need different success, pricing, and risk metrics. More evidence is needed that vendor-defined work units correlate with retained value and margin outside selected cohorts.

questions: If our primary model or data service disappeared in 30 days, which customer promise would fail first?
Where are we using one dashboard to compare fundamentally different automation jobs?
Which real-time intervention lacks a holdout, reversal path, or named owner?
